scenario: A technician wearing smart glasses assembles a mobile laser scanner (a survey device with a sensor head, lenses, caps, a body and mounting locks) following an expert's remote guidance.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a hand removing a protective cap from a scanner lens, not merely touching or holding the cap?
Does this video itself show a protective cap still covering a lens while the scanner head is being assembled, not a cap held beside an uncovered lens?
questions.why: Flags a cap that may have been left on during assembly.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a lens being inserted or screwed into the scanner head, not merely held near the head?
questions.why: Covers installation of an optical component.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show the sensor head being rotated until visible alignment marks on it and the body line up, not just the parts being brought together?
Does this video itself show the sensor head being seated onto the scanner body, not merely positioned above or beside it?
questions.why: Detects the main head-to-body assembly step.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show a hand turning or closing a mounting lock to secure the sensor head to the body, not merely touching the lock?
questions.why: Checks that the head is visibly secured.

questions.ask: Does this video itself show the mounting lock remaining visibly open or unlatched after the head is seated, not a lock that is being closed in the clip?
Does this video itself show the scanner body being fastened to its mount or support, not merely resting on or being held above it?
questions.why: Covers securing the assembled scanner for use.
